questions.answer: Context manager defines setup/cleanup around a block via __enter__ (entry, return -> as var) and __exit__ (exit, always runs even on error). `with` guarantees cleanup unlike manual open/close which leaks on exception.
questions.question: What is a context manager and why prefer `with open()` over manual close?

questions.answer: __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, tb) gets (None,None,None) on success else exception info. Return True suppresses, False/None propagates. Rarely suppress; just clean up.
questions.question: Explain __exit__'s three arguments and return-value semantics.

questions.answer: @contextmanager turns a generator into a manager: before yield=enter, yield value=as var, after yield=exit. Must wrap in try/finally for error-safe cleanup. Class-based better for stateful/complex reuse.
questions.question: How does @contextmanager work and when to use it vs a class?
Write class Connection manager printing open/use/close.
Write @contextmanager yielding 'Kakade session' with safe cleanup.
Write Timer manager printing elapsed time.

questions.answer: Cleanup after yield never ran because no try/finally — exception skips it. Fix with try: yield finally: cleanup. Similarly returning True from __exit__ swallows real bugs; default to None/False.
questions.question: Trap: @contextmanager cleanup skipped when block raises. Why and fix?

questions.answer: `as x` is __enter__'s return, not the manager — must `return self` or `yield conn`. Also `with open(a) as s, open(b,'w') as d:` handles both cleanups; nested form equivalent but verbose.
